facts.text: Bethel was first settled in 1774 and was originally named "Sudbury Canada" after settlers from Sudbury, Massachusetts who fought in the 1690 campaign.
The Lawrence Railroad opened in 1851, linking Bethel to Portland and later Montreal, turning the town into a hub for freight and summer tourists.
Founded in 1836, Gould Academy remains one of the Northeast's premier college‑preparatory schools, drawing students from across the region.
In 1897, the Maine Music Festival was founded in Bethel, and its founder brought Metropolitan Opera star Geraldine Farrar to perform in Odeon Hall.
An Abenaki village once stood on the north side of the Androscoggin River near Bethel, but it was abandoned before English settlement.
Large summer hotels sprang up on Bethel Hill in the 19th century, making the town a key stop for tourists heading to the White Mountains and Rangeley Lakes.
